paper.title_en: Coupled dark energy and apparent phantom crossing: a potential-independent lower bound
paper.abstract_en: Baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), combined with the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and type Ia supernovae, prefer a dark energy whose equation of state was below $-1$ in the past and is above $-1$ today. A canonical scalar field cannot cross this line, but it can appear to do so if it is coupled to dark matter, and we ask how strong this coupling must be, for any potential. We show that the apparent crossing requires the dark matter to lose a minimum fraction of its mass after recombination, fixed by the expansion history $H(z)$. For a constant coupling $β=d\ln m/dφ$, the mass can change only as fast as the field moves, and the speed of the field is itself set by $H(z)$, so that the coupling must be larger than a minimum value $β_{\rm min}[H(z)]$. This bound holds for any potential, applies to the largest value of the coupling when the coupling depends on the field, and is reached exactly when the field comes to rest within the observed range. For the DESI DR2 best fits, the dark matter must lose about 5-7% of its mass by $z\simeq 0.8$, which requires $β_{\rm min}=0.047$-$0.058$; including the uncertainties of the data, the public DESI DR2 chains give the 95% lower limit $|β|>0.025$-$0.038$. We also apply the bound to published fits of coupled quintessence: all of them respect it, and those with a constant coupling reproduce only a shallow version of the crossing. Since the coupling cannot be smaller than $β_{\rm min}$, two known effects of the coupling have a minimum size: an extra attraction between dark matter particles of at least a few tenths of a per cent of gravity, and a lensing signal at least a few per cent weaker than the clustering of dark matter would suggest.
